lead.purpose: The paragraph under a section heading.

label.purpose: Keycap legends and the version tag.

app-code.purpose: Code clips, the installer file name, colour values in the preview.

statement.purpose: The privacy band's statement, lit word by word.

close.purpose: The closing line above the last Download button.

question.purpose: FAQ questions; the hero lead from 1024px.

smartscreen-title.purpose: The depicted Windows SmartScreen dialog only.

shadows.name: app-window
shadows.purpose: Depicted app windows only (palette, preview, settings, tray menu, fragments). Dark: 0 18px 48px -14px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.7), 0 2px 8px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.4).

shadows.name: big-keycap
shadows.purpose: The Alt and V keys of the close.

shadows.name: button-edge
shadows.purpose: The primary button's bottom edge; the quiet button uses 0.06.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: State changes: buttons, underlines, rows, chevrons (100-250ms).

motion.name: ease-enter
motion.purpose: The hero entrance once on load: h1 rise 700ms, side fade-up 520ms, stage settle 900ms, keypress 360ms, palette open 260ms after 760ms; reopening later takes 180ms.

motion.name: statement-lit
motion.purpose: The privacy statement lights up word by word inside its own section (browsers with animation-timeline).

motion.name: autoplay
motion.value: type 'fig' from 1.3s, paste at 2.9s, reset at 4.3s
motion.purpose: The hero ritual, once, when the palette is 60% visible; stops on first pointer, key, focus, wheel or touch; never under reduced motion.

narrative.northStar: The Card Catalog in Windows 11 Material
narrative.overview: The site files Wincy the way Wincy files a clipboard. Every capability is a ruled record with a heading, a call number made of keycaps (the shortcut that calls it) and the real window it describes; label and value lists are tracings; kind filters are divider tabs; pins are signal flags. The cabinet is neutral Mica grey, the records are ruled entries rather than boxes, and the product itself appears as live HTML copies of its own windows sitting on a flat, hard-edged Windows wallpaper. Density is calm and one-section-per-screen on a laptop. The one ground change is the deep-blue privacy band. Motion is a single authored moment: the hero desktop opens on Alt+V, types, narrows, previews and pastes once, then hands control to the visitor.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral greys with no hue tint; one Windows-accent blue reserved for the chosen thing.
Schibsted Grotesk for the site's voice; Segoe UI Variable and Cascadia Mono for everything that depicts the app.
Real product UI, never illustrations: every window is a faithful copy of the app's components.
Keycaps as call numbers on records, rows of the shortcut list and the close.
Hairline rules organise records, shortcuts, questions and tracings.

rules.name: The Chosen Thing Rule
rules.body: Windows Accent Blue marks only what the visitor would choose or is choosing: the primary action, a link, a focus ring, the selected clip, the pressed filter. Nothing decorative is blue.

rules.name: The Logo-Only Gradient Rule
rules.body: The brand violet-to-teal lives in the logo tile and nowhere else: no hazes, glows, gradient text or tinted grounds.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Schibsted speaks for the site; Segoe UI and Cascadia speak for the app. Never set site copy in Cascadia, never set app UI in Schibsted.

rules.name: The One Axis Rule
rules.body: Every block hangs off the wrap's left edge and the grid's split line; nothing is centred in the page except windows on their wallpaper.

rules.name: The Depth Is The App Rule
rules.body: Only things that are windows in the real product cast shadows or blur. No site card, button or band gets elevation.

dos: Do depict the product only with faithful copies of its real components, using the app tokens and the Segoe UI / Cascadia faces.
Do file each capability as a ruled record under the keycaps that call it.
Do keep Windows Accent Blue for the primary action, links, focus and selection.
Do keep EN and ES in sync in src/i18n, with no copy in the components.
Do keep every moving thing optional: the autoplay stops on first touch and never runs under reduced motion.
donts: Don't use the brand violet or teal outside the logo: no haze, glow, gradient text or tinted grounds.
Don't put a box around a record or nest a card inside a card; windows sit on wallpaper, records are ruled.
Don't add shadows or blur to site elements; depth belongs to depicted windows.
Don't add illustrations, icon tiles, invented stats, testimonials or download counts.
